rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.read: USD-supportive: Dec hike ~85% priced (from ~80%), Oct ~18% — the hawkish hold is in week five; CPI Wed 7:30am CT is the test, Warsh speaks Thu 10:30pm CT.

sources.label: Reuters: Global markets wrapup (Dec 85%, Oct 18%) — Oct 12

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: US resilient, Canada cracking, China reopening soft — the growth gaps all favor the dollar; US investment-grade credit spreads at their widest since the Iran war began.

sources.label: Reuters: Canada's employment surprisingly shrinks in September

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: Headline risk, core watch — US CPI Wed 7:30am CT (consensus ~3.6% y/y; the key number is core m/m at 0.2%), the last big print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.read: The reopen priced the war then sold it — Brent $105.48 → ~$103.4 on ceasefire-and-diesel supply hopes; DXY ~102.2 near 18-mo highs; CBA expects Houthi attacks on Saudi energy assets to continue.

sources.label: WSJ: Oil falls on Russian diesel hopes (Oct 11)

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.read: The ~$13 Brent–WTI spread keeps the geopolitical-premium gauge wide; WTI ~$90.50 is the CAD read; Goldman sees ~$20/bbl of premium with Dec Brent at $90.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Yen longs rebuilt to 62,325 into escalation; crowded USD longs vs stretched EUR shorts — a soft CPI would squeeze the dollar crowd hardest.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.read: French budget plenary Tuesday 3:00am CT is the live fuse on the OAT–Bund spread (~140–146bp); the euro waits.
